new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for leng1260, so this is the first evidence rather than an agreement or contradiction. It is consistent with the areal Dayic picture in Mortensen 2021 (Kemaloh Lun Bawang stress 'not contrastive and.. usually [on] a word's final syllable', §3.4 p. 51; a shift to 'heavy stress on the ultima' reconstructed for the Ulu Padi dialects, p. 224). The item record lists only the PDF and four JPEG page scans — there is no audio for Lengilu' in the collection, and a REST search of ScholarSpace for 'Lengilu' returns only CM1-003, CM1-004, the dissertation and the collection record; no later Mortensen publication on Lengilu' surfaced there. Not a citab…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Unpublished field transcriptions only: in the Lengilu' (Long Layu' / Long Padi) wordlist the stress mark sits on the final syllable of nearly every polysyllable (la'waɪ, i'kɔh, da'ʔət, kəmə'kar, la'wɪd, da'ŋaɪ, tu'ŋaɪ, ba'ʔʊŋ, tə'fuh, pə'hũŋ, la'ʔʊd, ka'mih, ki'təh, mu'juh, i'dəh, mə'laɪt, mə'sɪŋ, ma'daw, la'ʔih, ma'taj, de'ʔɔn, mu'ləʔ, bu'rəʔ, na'ŋəʔ), the fieldworker writes 'Final stress?' beside the monosyllabic 1sg [ak] and 'But w/ final stress' beside ngirup 'drink', and in the companion notebook notes [i'kəh] 2sg in Lengilu' and the loss of the unstressed initial syllable of enun 'what' (nun/non) in the Krayan, esp. Long Layu'. Nowhere is a rule stated in prose.
new_statements.exceptions: p. 3 padé 'rice' is written [pádaɪ] (LL) / [pedaɪ] (LP) with an accent on the first vowel, the only possibly non-final mark; p. 1 berek [bərək] carries the query 'stress?'; p. 1 1sg [ak] 'Final stress?' is a query about a monosyllable. The explicit prose statements in CM1-003 — p. 22 'Pa' Padi.. Definitely word-final stress.' and p. 29 'Tang Paye.. Strong final stress.' — are about Pa' Padi (Ulu Padi group) and Tang Paye (Sa'ban-like), which Mortensen does NOT classify as Lengilu'; p. 49 'Revised theory of stress: Final if: penultimate vowel is /ə/ and final is not.. Otherwise penultimate' is about Kemaloh Lun Bawang at Long Semadoh.
new_statements.identity_note: CM1-004 records 'Lengilu'' as the Long Layu' (LL) and Long Padi (LP) dialects of the Krayan, Kalimantan Utara (speakers Lewi Gala' Paru 'LG' and his daughter Avalari 'A'); Mortensen 2021 §11.4.3 defines the Lengilu' group as Long Layu', Long Padi, Binuang and the former Long Mutan, and excludes Ba' Liku (Clayre 2005's 'Lengilo'') on phonological grounds; the notebook itself warns that Binuang is 'originally Lengilu' but mixed now'. The three unopened UNIMAS works describe 'Lengilo' as spoken among Lun Bawang at Lawas / Ba'Kelalan, Sarawak (Malaysian side), whose identity with the Krayan Lengilu' of Glottolog leng1260 is unverified.

sources.note: The only phonological description of a variety called Lengilo (consonant/vowel/diphthong inventories from one 80-year-old speaker); a 'deskripsi awal' in Malay would normally include a tekanan (stress) note. Identity caveat: speakers live among Lun Bawang at Lawas/Ba'Kelalan, Sarawak, and the companion study finds 94.6% lexical identity with Lun Bawang, so this may not be the Krayan Lengilu' of leng1260.
